title: Monetary Policy Report—April 2025
summary: The Bank of Canada held its policy rate steady at 2.75% in April 2025, as the economy showed strength at end-2024 but faced growing uncertainty from escalating US tariffs and trade conflict. The Governing Council assessed that while inflation was near the 2% target, trade uncertainty and tariffs were expected to slow growth while adding price pressures. The report outlined two illustrative scenarios for US trade policy outcomes given the unpredictability of tariff shifts.
key_points: Bank of Canada maintained the overnight rate target at 2.75%, with the Bank Rate at 3% and deposit rate at 2.70%.
Canadian economy ended 2024 strong, with inflation near the 2% target in Q4 2024.
US has imposed large and broad-based tariffs on Canada and most trading partners, with many tariffs remaining in place.
Trade uncertainty and tariffs are expected to slow economic growth and add to price pressures.
Removal of the consumer carbon tax will temporarily lower inflation and cause a one-time reduction in consumer price levels, primarily affecting gasoline prices.
Canada's neutral interest rate range is estimated between 2.25% and 3.25%, with potential output growth anticipated to slow.
Global economic growth was solid at end-2024, with inflation easing toward central bank targets before tariff escalation.
why_it_matters: This quarterly report defines the Bank of Canada's official assessment of the Canadian economy and its forward policy stance. For traders and analysts, the policy rate decision (2.75% held) and the Governing Council's characterization of trade conflict risks inform expectations for future rate moves. The report's scenario analysis for US tariff paths is critical for gauging the range of potential outcomes for Canadian GDP growth and inflation.
macro_context: The report was written during a period of escalating US-Canada trade tensions. US tariff impositions on Canadian goods were creating uncertainty about both economic growth (through reduced exports) and price pressures (through higher input costs). The Bank characterized the outlook as 'highly uncertain' given the unpredictability of US trade policy direction, speed, and magnitude of shifts.
